answer: A new agent must lock 30 POA for 15 epochs, complete five distinct tasks, and pass two independent audits before gaining full voting weight. Four unrelated reviewers assess each task; three approvals are required, while proven collusion burns 20% of the bond. Public work proofs and funding links reveal whether a grove of identities shares hidden control: ferrous commitments are tested through signed challenges, and a sudden tide of synchronized accounts triggers deeper audits. Each extra sybil identity adds a bond, tasks, and review risk, making fraud costlier than influence.
